prompt:
Cardinal is holding our summer creator slots until Monday, after that they go out to other brands, so I need a recommendation in front of Grace before that lapses. Robert has already made his mind up in the sales channel, and I would rather not argue with him from a position of having a feeling about it.

The pilot closed on the fifteenth and Cardinal sent their wrap through the next morning. It reads beautifully, which is what a wrap report is for, and it is not the thing I am going to sign a summer flight on. Every lead that pilot produced landed in our own records tagged back to whoever sent it, so what each of those five actually delivered is something I can check rather than take from the agency's version of it.

So work it through properly. What we paid each of them, what came back, and what happened to any of it after it came back. Take the paid side out of our own books rather than off Renee's summary, because the two have drifted before and I am not signing a second flight on her arithmetic. The handful that made it to closing earned us something on the back end, and I want that in there too, because Grace will ask what the pilot returned and not only what it cost. I do not want a cost per view. I want to know what it cost us to put an actual file on the board, and how much of what came in we were ever in a position to do anything with.

Denise reviewed the pilot content a week or so back and came back with something I have to respect, and Grace put a condition on the money when she released it that limits how I am allowed to commit it. Neither is negotiable, so wherever you land has to survive both.

While you are in there, a piece of what came in was never ours to work and it is still sitting open in the pipeline where the loan officers keep picking it up and burning a morning on it. Close that out so nobody wastes another call, and only that. The live ones stay where they are.

Then the recommendation. Who we keep for the summer, who we let go, and what that spend looks like against what I have been given to spend. If it cuts against Robert, say so and give me the reason I can hand him, because he will ask for one.

Send it up to Grace with Denise copied, put the outcome on the record in the CRM against Cardinal and against each of the five individually, because in September nobody will remember why we passed on the ones we passed on, and come back to Robert in the sales channel so he is not still waiting on me.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that the amount Keystone was billed for the creator pilot totals $19,500.
criteria.evidence: See OE 15. The Agent states a total pilot spend of $21,000.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks what was paid to each creator and directs that the paid side be taken from Keystone's own books. The billed total across the sixteen Cardinal bills is the figure that answers it.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that Tasha Bell (@tashatalksmoney) cost Keystone $6,000 across the creator pilot.
criteria.evidence: See OE 15. The Agent states $7,500 as the pilot cost for @tashatalksmoney.
criteria.cb_justification: Her true cost is the fact that reframes the whole comparison, since every stakeholder argument in the universe is built on the lower agency-quoted figure.

criteria.criterion: The Agent determines that Keystone is licensed to originate loans in North Carolina only.
criteria.evidence: See OE 5. The Agent states the North Carolina only licensing limit.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks how much of the incoming volume Keystone was ever in a position to act on. That question cannot be answered without the licensing footprint.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that 15 of the 49 leads produced by the creator pilot are located outside North Carolina and cannot be originated by Keystone.
criteria.evidence: See OE 11 and OE 12. The Agent states that 15 of 49 pilot leads are out of footprint.
criteria.cb_justification: This is the quantified answer to how much of the delivered volume was workable, and it separates raw lead counts from usable ones.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that 13 of the 18 leads attributed to @tashatalksmoney are located outside North Carolina, leaving 5 that Keystone could work.
criteria.evidence: See OE 12. The Agent gives the out-of-footprint split for @tashatalksmoney.
criteria.cb_justification: The creator with the largest apparent delivery is the one whose delivery collapses under the footprint test. This is the central data trap in the task.

criteria.evidence: See OE 16 and OE 17. The Agent attributes 4 funded loan(s) to @clthomeguy.
criteria.cb_justification: Funded files are the outcome Grace states she is measuring on, so attribution of each funded loan to its originating creator is load bearing for the decision.

criteria.evidence: See OE 20. The Agent states a cost per funded loan of approximately $1,125 for @clthomeguy.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states that the cost per workable North Carolina lead for @tashatalksmoney was approximately $1,200.00.
criteria.evidence: See OE 20. The Agent states a cost per workable lead of approximately $1,500 for @tashatalksmoney.
criteria.cb_justification: Applying the footprint to the spend is what exposes the gap between apparent and real delivery, and it needs the corrected $7,500 cost rather than the quoted fee.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies @clthomeguy as having the lowest cost per funded loan of the five pilot creators.
criteria.evidence: See OE 20. The Agent ranks @clthomeguy first on cost per funded loan.
criteria.cb_justification: The recommendation rests on a ranking, so the ranking itself has to be stated rather than left implicit in a table of figures.

criteria.criterion: The Agent determines that Priya Raman (@firsthomepriya) is not available for the summer flight because the Regulation Z advertising finding against her content is unremediated and cannot be cleared before the June 1 start.
criteria.evidence: See OE 5 and OE 21. The Agent excludes @firsthomepriya on the unremediated compliance finding.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt states that Denise's finding is not negotiable. This is the constraint that removes the second best performer on return, which is what makes the decision hard rather than arithmetic.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states that the summer rate of $30,000 for @tashatalksmoney exceeds the entire $27,000 released for the flight.
criteria.evidence: See OE 6 and OE 21. The Agent compares the $30,000 rate against the $27,000 budget.
criteria.cb_justification: Even setting performance aside, the creator Robert is pushing for is unaffordable, which is an independent and decisive reason to release her.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states that the $27,000 released for the summer flight has to be committed in full by May 4, 2026 or it reverts to the general marketing line.
criteria.evidence: See OE 7 and OE 21. The Agent states the full commitment condition and the deadline.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says Grace put a condition on the money that limits how it may be committed. The all or nothing condition is what forces one exact combination.
